[[Image:Schlierenfoto Mach 1-2 Pfeilflügel - NASA.jpg|thumb|right|Petrovsky lacunas are similar to the spaces between [[shock wave]]s of a [[supersonic]] object.]]
{{Other uses|Lacuna (disambiguation){{!}}Lacuna}}
In mathematics, a '''Petrovsky lacuna''', named for the Russian mathematician [[I. G. Petrovsky]], is a region where the [[fundamental solution]] of a linear [[hyperbolic partial differential equation]] vanishes. 
They were studied by {{harvtxt|Petrovsky|1945}} who found [[topological]] conditions for their existence.

Petrovsky's work was generalized and updated by {{harvs|txt|last1=Atiyah|last2=Bott|last3=Gårding|year1= 1970|year2=1973}}.
